Notes: Dhakal p. 47 prints /dauri/ “cord for tethering beast.” Turner6225 gives Hindi daurī “rope to which a string of cattle are fastened,” Nepali ḍori “rope, tether” and regional ḍorī/ḍori “rope.” The unnasalised daur-i shape and precise cattle-tether sense favor this article over the nasal dãurī branch under 6283. Darai pp. 47, 51, 55; source PDF and full CDIAL reviewed; no rebuild

Dhakal p. 47 prints /dʰoulə/ “washed.” Turner6886 gives Prakrit dhō(v)aï “washes,” Nepali dhunu, Maithili dhoeb and Bhojpuri dhowal; Darai -lə is the source-described past ending, leaving the corresponding dʰou- washing stem. Turner6833 itself places Nepali dhunu probably under 6886. Darai pp. 47, 51, 55; source PDF and full CDIAL reviewed; no rebuild

Dhakal p. 51 prints /par/ “across/COND.PART”; the installed record retains the “across” sense. Turner8100 explicitly gives Kumaoni par “at a distance,” Nepali pār “on the other side of” and Maithili/Hindi pār “across.” This assignment addresses the spatial sense only; the source’s conditional-particle use may be a separate grammatical development. Darai pp. 47, 51, 55; source PDF and full CDIAL reviewed; no rebuild

Dhakal p. 55 prints /nanʰi/ “small” among breathy-nasal examples. Turner12732 gives Prakrit laṇha “small,” Punjabi nannhā and Hindi nānh/nānhā “small,” plus Maithili nānhiṭā “childhood.” These comparanda support the Darai nanʰ- stem despite the wider ślakṣṇa family’s multiple regional shapes.
